description:
FOUND s490 (Fable) from the CPAN board re-measured for the README (Safe-Isa t/safe_isa.t #45 `is_deeply([ $foo->$_can("bar") ], [ undef ])`, a row that became VISIBLE when the file stopped stopping at row 8).  Minimised, perl 5.40.3 vs main 2233f51c:

  package Foo; sub new { bless {}, shift }  package main;  my $o = Foo->new;
  sub r1 { my $x = shift; return $x->can(@_) }               my @a = r1($o, "nope");        # perl 1   PCL 0
  sub r2 { my ($x,$m) = (shift,shift); return $x->$m(@_) }   my @b = r2($o, "can", "nope"); # perl 1   PCL 0
  sub r3 { my ($x,$m) = (shift,shift); $x->$m(@_) }          (no `return`)                    # perl 1   PCL 0
  sub r4 { my $x = shift; return $x->isa("Nope") }           my @f = r4($o);                  # 1 on both (isa answers a defined "")
  my @d = ($o->can("nope"));                                 DIRECT call in a list             # 1 on both

So the value is right where the call sits in a list itself and LOST when it is a sub's result: `can`'s false is CL NIL, and NIL crossing the return protocol in list context is "no values" -- the same class #403 (s473t6b) closed for the filetests ("NIL is not a perl value: it leaves ZERO values where perl leaves ONE").

DO NOT fix it by making `p-can` return *p-undef*: the runtime calls p-can itself and tests the answer as a CL boolean (`(let ((prop (p-can err "PROPAGATE"))) (if prop ...` in %p-die-reuse-eval-error, and the overload / DESTROY / AUTOLOAD lookups) -- *p-undef* is TRUE in CL.  The perl-visible boundary is the method-call dispatch for the name `can` (and UNIVERSAL::can); that is where a NIL becomes perl's undef.  AUDIT THE FAMILY while there: which other perl-visible builtins answer CL NIL for false (grep the dispatch for UNIVERSAL methods, `ref`-less `blessed`, `fileno` on a closed handle, `wantarray`)? -- probe each as `sub r { return BUILTIN }` in list context vs perl.

Probes: the scratchpad shapes above are complete; guard file Pl/t/filetest-stack-01.t section 5 is the #403 sibling, a `universal-01.t` row set is the natural home.  `cl/` change: sweep + op/ + mro/ companion legs.

=== DONE (s491a) ===

SHIPPED.  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only; guard Pl/t/universal-01.t (4 rows, 1.0 s
wall), 3 of them FAIL on an extraction of 337f6a23.

THE FIX IS #403's SHAPE: ONE returner, no new state.

  (defun %p-can-answer (invocant &rest args)
    (or (apply #'p-can invocant args) *p-undef*))

routed from the FIVE perl-visible boundaries and nowhere else: the four
dispatch arms that serve the method NAME `can` (the qualified-method arm, the
class-name arm, the object arm and the SUPER:: fallback) and UNIVERSAL::pl-can.
`p-can` itself is UNCHANGED and still answers NIL, because the runtime asks it
as a CL boolean and *p-undef* is TRUE in CL -- the task's own warning, verified
by the guard's fourth row (die-PROPAGATE and AUTOLOAD, both `can`-shaped
lookups, unmoved).

THE FAMILY AUDIT (perl 5.40.3 vs main 337f6a23; probe
scratch/s491a/probes/p1912.pl, each `sub r { return BUILTIN }` called in LIST
context, n = elements, d = definedness of the first):

  shape                                        perl      PCL before   verdict
  $x->can("nope")            (method)          n=1 undef n=0          BUG
  $x->$m(@_) with $m="can"   (dynamic name)    n=1 undef n=0          BUG
  ... the same without `return`                n=1 undef n=0          BUG
  Foo->can("nope")           (class name)      n=1 undef n=0          BUG
  UNIVERSAL::can($x,"nope")  (function)        n=1 undef n=0          BUG
  $x->can("real")            (a HIT)           n=1 CODE  n=1 CODE     ok
  $x->isa("Nope")                              n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  UNIVERSAL::isa($x,"Nope")                    n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  $x->DOES("Nope")                             n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  ref("plain")                                 n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  defined(undef)                               n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  "x" =~ /y/                                   n=0       n=0          ok (perl
                                                                      gives the
                                                                      EMPTY list)
  exists $ENV{nope}                            n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  delete $h{nope}                              n=1 undef n=1 undef    ok
  wantarray                                    n=1 def   n=1 def      ok
  ($o->can("nope"))          DIRECT, in a list n=1       n=1          ok
  the Safe::Isa $_can idiom                    n=1 undef n=0          BUG

So `can` is the WHOLE family -- five spellings of one lookup, no second member
to fix or file.  `isa`/`DOES` were closed by #1737 (boolean-valued, 1 or "");
the filetests by #403; a failed match's EMPTY list is perl's own.

THE OTHER DIRECTION, probed (scratch/s491a/probes/p1912b.pl, 13 rows, ALL
identical to perl): the new false is still false in boolean, negated,
defined-or, string and numeric context; a HIT is still a callable CODE ref
through both spellings; `can` on a class name, an unblessed ref, an unknown
package and undef all stay undef; overload still resolves ("" and + handlers
both fire); grep/map/hash-value/list-assignment over `can` behave as perl.

PERF (the task's ask: `can` is on Moo/Role::Tiny's hot path).  INTERLEAVED
bench A/B, BENCH_K=5, 337f6a23 extraction vs this tree, `moo-objs`:
pass 1 base 1.6820 s / fix 1.5407 s = -8.4 % (load 4.8 -> 2.8).  An earlier
NON-interleaved pair read base 1.8478 / fix 2.7253 on a box at load 5.5 with a
sibling agent running -- box noise, not the change: nothing in it can cost 0.9 s
at N=20,000, and the interleaved pass reversed the sign.  The batch's other
runtime touch (member 2's %p-symref-name) is DECLAIMED INLINE and every caller
asks it after its own hot arm; p-ensure-hashref's `hash-table-p` arm was hoisted
to FIRST while there (a hash table is neither a string nor a number nor a glob,
so no arm below can want it).
subject: SILENT WRONG: a FALSE `can` that is a sub's RETURN VALUE leaves ZERO values in list context -- `sub r { return $x->can("nope") } my @a = r();` is 1 element (undef) in perl and EMPTY in PCL (the Safe::Isa `$_can` idiom; safe_isa.t row 45)
